---
title: "Cloudflare Account Migration"
date: 2026-09-28
---

::: {.callout-note}
## Status: plan, deferred
The `bioconductor.org` zone went into the **current** Cloudflare account (the personal
account `55bf7202…`, which already holds the `bioc-site` Worker, Workers Paid and R2 Paid)
so the DNS cutover did not wait on an account move. See the
[DNS cutover runbook](dns-cutover.qmd#migration-plan). This page is the plan for moving
everything to a dedicated Bioconductor account **after** the cutover has settled. It has
not been rehearsed, and items marked *verify* have not been confirmed against Cloudflare.
:::

## Why move

The Worker, R2 buckets, dev hostname and now the production zone share an account with
unrelated personal domains.

- **Permissions are account-wide.** Workers and R2 rights can't be scoped to one
  project, so a Bioconductor co-admin would hold rights over unrelated infrastructure,
  and the reverse.
- **Billing, grants and sponsorships attach to an account.** Bioconductor's bill should
  not be one person's card.
- **Bus factor.** A project account with 2–3 super administrators survives any one
  person leaving. A personal account doesn't.

## What it costs to do later instead of first

Doing it after the cutover means a **second nameserver change on the live production <!-- docs-check: ok -->
domain**. A zone can't be handed between accounts. It's added fresh to the new
account, which assigns different nameservers, and the registrar is repointed. That is
the price of not blocking the cutover. It's manageable because the zone is small, fully
scripted, and the procedure below keeps both accounts serving identical answers
throughout.

## Inventory — what moves, and how

It's a redeploy, not a rebuild. Everything except data is declared in `wrangler.jsonc`.

| Piece | Effort | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Workers, cron triggers, Workflows: `bioc-site` (cron every 15 min, Workflow `bioc-release-roll`), `bioc-registry` (cron every 15 min, Workflow `bioc-registry-observe`), and `bioc-prop`, now a stub that only returns a 301 to bioc-registry | minutes | Redeploy with the new `account_id`; code unchanged |
| Secrets, API tokens | ~1 hour | Nothing transfers. Re-set every secret, reissue CI tokens, update GitHub Actions secrets |
| R2 buckets `bioc-site`, `bioc-prop` (now bioc-registry's archive bucket) | ~1 day, mostly waiting | No cross-account move. Copy with Super Slurper or rclone. Egress is free; cost is write operations, driven by object count: `bioc-site` holds 4.2 million objects, 5.1 TB ([costs](improvements.qmd#costs-about-5000-a-month-down-to-a-couple-of-hundred)); `bioc-prop` not yet counted |
| Producers writing to R2 | 1–2 hours | The S3 endpoint embeds the account ID. Every sync job needs the new endpoint and keys, and the purge token needs access to the new zone. `cf-purge.sh` in bioc-edge purges four hosts: `bioconductor.org`, `www.`, `next.` and `bioc-dev.cancerdatasci.org` |
| Analytics Engine dataset `bioc_site_requests_v3` | not movable | History restarts (retention is ~3 months anyway) |
| Logpush job (request log, [ADR 0003](adr/0003-request-logging-after-the-cloudflare-cutover.md)) | minutes | Recreate. **Overlap old and new jobs** so no window goes unlogged; Logpush cannot backfill |
| In-flight Workflow instances | lost | Let them finish, or accept a rerun |
| `bioconductor.org` zone | ~1 hour + a registrar change | Below |
| Zone settings (SSL mode, Always Use HTTPS, Bot Preference Sync off, cache rules…) | ~1 hour | Not copied. List them from the old zone first. Known so far: Browser Cache TTL "Respect existing headers" (set 2026-09-28, [bioc-edge#38](https://github.com/seandavi/bioc-edge/issues/38)), and the WAF rule blocking AS150436 and AS4229 on `/talks/` ([bioc-edge#32](https://github.com/seandavi/bioc-edge/issues/32)). Without that rule, the crawler that hit `/talks/` on 2026-09-28 is served again |
| Edge certificate | automatic, but see the gap below | Issued fresh for the new zone |

## Procedure

### A. Prepare the new account (no user impact)

1. Create the account under a Bioconductor-owned address. Add at least two more super
   administrators, and set the billing owner and payment method.
2. Subscribe **Workers Paid** and **R2** on it.
3. Create the R2 buckets and start the copy. Record object counts on both sides.
4. Deploy the Workers to the new account with a **temporary hostname** only (a
   `workers.dev` name, or a spare domain). Re-set secrets. Run the full-crawl
   `cutover-diff.sh` against it.
5. Repoint producers to write to **both** accounts' buckets, or to the new one plus a
   final re-sync before the switch. Both Workers must serve the same bytes during the
   overlap in step C.

### B. Build the zone in the new account (no user impact)

1. Export the live zone from the **old** Cloudflare account:
   **DNS → Records → Import and Export → Export**, or
   `GET /zones/<id>/dns_records/export`. Cloudflare is now the source of truth, not
   Route53. Also save the record list as JSON through the API, because the BIND export
   does not carry each record's **proxied** flag.
2. Add `bioconductor.org` to the new account and choose the zone-file upload. It gets
   its own pending nameserver pair.
3. **Reset proxy status record by record** from the JSON. The dashboard upload marks
   every A/CNAME as Proxied (seen on 2026-09-28). Only the records that are proxied in the
   old zone should be proxied here (on 2026-09-30: apex, `www` and `next`).
4. Recreate zone settings from the list above, and the Worker routes for
   `bioconductor.org/*`, `www.bioconductor.org/*` and `next.bioconductor.org/*` in the new
   account's `wrangler.jsonc` (inert until the zone is Active).
5. Diff the two Cloudflare zones with the repo's script:
   ```sh
   A=<old-cf-ns> B=<new-cf-ns> ./dns/verify-zone.sh
   ```
   Refresh `dns/route53-index.txt` from the old zone's export first if records changed
   since the Route53 copy.
6. The new zone is pending, so the 28-day clock runs (Free plan). Do C within that window.

### The certificate gap

A pending zone has no active edge certificate. At the moment of the switch, resolvers
that reach the new zone for a **proxied** name (apex, `www`) are served by a zone
whose Universal certificate isn't issued yet. That means TLS errors until it is,
usually minutes and occasionally longer. Two ways to close the gap:

- **Pre-issue.** Order an Advanced Certificate for `bioconductor.org` and
  `*.bioconductor.org` in the new zone with **TXT** validation, then add the TXT
  challenge records to the *old* (live) zone so it validates before the switch.
  *Verify* that Advanced Certificate Manager allows this on a pending zone and what it
  costs. It is a paid add-on.
- **Drop to grey for the switch.** If CloudFront is still running (before M2 retires
  it), set apex and `www` back to DNS only in the old zone for the switch window. The <!-- docs-check: ok -->
  site is then served by CloudFront (the rollback target of the site flip). Re-proxy in
  the new zone once its certificate shows Active. This is free, but only available
  while CloudFront exists. **If the account move happens after M2, the pre-issue route
  is the only one.**

### C. Switch nameservers

1. Lower nothing: Cloudflare's NS TTL is fixed at 86400 s, and the .org parent's is
   3600 s.
2. Freeze record changes in both Cloudflare zones, or make each change in both.
3. Registrar (Route53 Domains, AWS account 555219204010): **Registered domains →
   bioconductor.org → Actions → Edit name servers** → replace the old Cloudflare pair
   with the new pair. Copy, don't type.
4. Cloudflare (new account) → **Overview → Re-check now**. Wait for Active and the
   certificate.
5. The old zone turns **Moved** (Cloudflare: deleted after 7 days in that state). It
   keeps answering for resolvers that cached the old delegation, for up to a day.
   **Keep the old Worker, routes, buckets and Logpush running for at least 2 days**, so
   those stragglers get the same site and are still logged.
6. Post-checks: `verify-zone.sh` against the public resolvers, `curl -sI` apex and `www`,
   mail to and from the domain, `ssh git@git.bioconductor.org`, `cutover-diff.sh`, and
   Logpush records arriving in the new destination.

**Rollback** (within the 7-day Moved window): put the old Cloudflare pair back at the
registrar, then **Re-check now** in the old account. *Verify* that a Moved zone
re-activates in place rather than needing a re-add. If it doesn't, the rollback is
re-adding it and re-importing from the saved export, which would mean new nameservers
again. Don't let the old zone reach Deleted until the new one has run clean for a week.

### D. Clean up (after a clean week)

- Remove the zone from the old account, then the Workers, routes, buckets, tokens and
  Logpush job there.
- Retire the dev hostname `bioc-dev.cancerdatasci.org`, or recreate it under a
  Bioconductor-owned name.
- Update the docs that name the old account ID (this page and the
  [DNS cutover runbook](dns-cutover.qmd)).
  [ADR 0003](adr/0003-request-logging-after-the-cloudflare-cutover.md) names no account.

## Open questions

- Who owns the new account and who are the super administrators? Who pays? Not decided
  as of 2026-09-30. Until then everything runs on, and is billed to, the personal account
  named at the top of this page.
- R2 object count for `bioc-prop`, to size the copy.
- Is the move done before or after M2 retires CloudFront? That decides how the
  certificate gap is closed.
- Is there a sponsorship route (e.g. Cloudflare's open-source program) that should be
  applied for on the new account before any paid add-ons?
